project.title: Aquarium hall generated pixel materials v3
project.description: Replace smooth placeholder hall surfaces with three generated pixel-art material sources. Preserve editable parcels, tanks, partitions, collision, saves and all existing tank artwork.
project.art_direction: Create actual hand-painted PIXEL ART material artwork matching the supplied accepted fish illustration: deliberate crisp square pixel clusters, restrained natural colors and coherent painted material changes. Design on a 256 by 256 logical pixel grid enlarged exactly 4x to a native 1024 by 1024 image. The pixel clusters must be visible and purposeful, not fine photographic grain, random noise or smooth gradients. This is a full-bleed seamless square ALBEDO TEXTURE for an editable 3D aquarium hall, seen perpendicular to its surface. All four edges must tile continuously. Flat neutral diffuse illumination, no perspective, no ambient occlusion, no cast shadows, no bevelled 3D preview, no sphere, no borders, no background, no labels or lettering. The input fish controls pixel illustration finish only; do not copy the fish, its silhouette or scales.
project.gameplay_loop: Expand standardized indoor parcels and place tanks and partitions in a hall with the same pixel illustration finish as its exhibits.
project.session_goal: Inspect generated floor, wall and bench timber artwork, then compare in actual Godot hall and close first-person views.
project.visual_reference_usage: North-star full-screen mock at project viewport resolution (1024x1024). Align palette, line weight, and mood with art_direction — not pixel-perfect. Do NOT use as img2img input for character/icon sprites; those use assets[].display_size on white studio.

asset.name: hall_wall
asset.description:
Painted pale limestone-gray mineral plaster for a welcoming aquarium interior. An uninterrupted wall finish, NOT bricks, blocks or floor tiles. Readable small groups of square brush marks, broad subtle cool gray paint variations, occasional restrained pixel scratches. Mid-light neutral albedo so engine tint can produce cream or teal walls. No strong directional lighting, bold cracks, mold, high-contrast camouflage or isolated single-pixel noise. Complete repeat covers 2 by 2 meters.
